A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original IFEval and ComplexBench experiments, mitigation comparisons, case studies, attention analyses, and reasoning-length correlations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, although GPT-4o-mini results are removed.

M1.justification: The four mitigation procedures—few-shot learning, self-reflection, self-selective reasoning, and classifier-selective reasoning—are unchanged. Their prompt templates, classifier formulation, and inference procedures remain the same.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same IFEval and English-compatible ComplexBench data and instruction-following tasks. Removing an evaluated language model does not change the represented datasets, languages, or task requirements.

E2.justification: The comparison methods remain Original/non-CoT, CoT, and the same four mitigation strategies; Table 2 also retains the same reasoning/non-reasoning pairs. GPT-4o-mini is removed as a target model on which these strategies are evaluated, rather than as a distinct comparison strategy.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation model suite shrinks: GPT-4o-mini disappears from Section 3.2 and Table 1, reducing that table from 14 target models to 13. Dataset sizes, metrics, temperature, classifier splits, and training settings remain unchanged for the retained evaluations.

E4.justification: Appendix G's Figure 9 removes GPT-4o-mini's diagnostics of whether self-selected reasoning matches actual benefit, and Appendix I removes its reasoning-length correlation analysis. The remaining diagnostics, four case studies, and attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The statistical reporting practices are unchanged, including attention-distribution summaries and Pearson correlations. Neither version introduces additional repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; deleting model-specific estimates changes results rather than the estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 removes GPT-4o-mini's baseline and mitigation scores, including Original/CoT accuracies of 82.6/76.9 on IFEval and 66.5/60.3 on ComplexBench. Its Figure 9 results and Table 3 correlations of 0.034 and 0.227 are also removed. Retained numerical results and plotted values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The transformer-attention formulas, constraint-attention definitions, Equations 1–2, and attention-drop calculation are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that explicit reasoning can impair instruction following, that attention shifts help explain failures, and that selective reasoning can recover performance. The claimed novelty and four contributions are not redefined.

C2.justification: The explanations of reasoning-induced failures and mitigation effectiveness remain unchanged. Both versions retain the qualifications about uncontrolled reasoning-model comparisons, few-shot example bias, computational overhead, and the study's restriction to instruction-following tasks.

D1.justification: v3 deletes v1's page-2 footnote providing a code-and-data repository link, without replacement access information. Hardware, prompt examples, classifier hyperparameters, and grid-search details remain unchanged. This establishes loss of access documentation, not that the external resources ceased to exist.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to prior reasoning and instruction-following research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to the model-list deletion, removed access footnote, some plot-label capitalization, and the version header. The substantive prose, section order, and appendix organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 3 and 9 are redrawn without GPT-4o-mini, with changes to label orientation, spacing, and axis labeling. Tables 1 and 3 lose rows, and Tables 1 and 2 move earlier through pagination changes. The remaining graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 removes the documented code/data access route and some empirical evidence without resolving the accompanying numerical summaries. Section 3.4 still reports declines for '13 out of 14' models, although the revised Table 1 shows 12 declines among 13 models. The modest presentation changes do not outweigh this loss of reproducibility documentation and internal consistency, while the central scientific content remains intact.
